---
id: c-m2-sensor-codec
title: Compressing Sensor Logs with Delta, ZigZag and Varints
difficulty: Hard
order: 3
tags: bit manipulation, dynamic buffers, encoding, error handling
time_limit: 2
---
## Statement
Robot sensor logs are long sequences of slowly changing integers (encoder ticks, temperatures, timestamps). Compress them the way Protocol Buffers and time-series databases do:

1. **Delta encoding:** store the first value, then the differences `v[i] - v[i-1]`.
2. **ZigZag:** map signed integers to unsigned ones so small magnitudes stay small: `0→0, -1→1, 1→2, -2→3, 2→4, …`, i.e. `(n << 1) ^ (n >> 63)` for 64-bit `n`.
3. **Varint (LEB128):** write each unsigned value 7 bits at a time, least significant group first. The high bit (`0x80`) of each byte means "more bytes follow".

Compressed format: varint(count), then varint(zigzag(v[0])), then varint(zigzag(delta)) for each subsequent value.

Commands (one per line):
- `encode N v1 ... vN` (values are 64-bit signed; deltas are computed with wrap-around in `uint64_t` arithmetic, so even `INT64_MIN` to `INT64_MAX` works): print the encoded bytes as lowercase hex, followed by ` (B bytes, R%)`, where R is the size relative to 8·N raw bytes, rounded to an integer. For N = 0, print `00 (1 bytes, 0%)`.
- `decode HEX`: decode and print the values separated by spaces (an empty line for zero values), or one of: `error: odd hex length`, `error: bad hex digit`, `error: truncated` (the data ends in the middle of a varint, or before `count` values are read), `error: varint too long` (more than 10 bytes, or the 10th byte > 1), `error: trailing bytes`.

## Starter
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

int main(void) {
    char cmd[16];
    while (scanf("%15s", cmd) == 1) {
    }
    return 0;
}
```

## Hints
- Use `uint64_t` everywhere for deltas: `uint64_t d = (uint64_t)v[i] - (uint64_t)v[i-1];` wraps around safely (signed overflow would be UB). Then treat `d` as signed for ZigZag: `zz = (d << 1) ^ (uint64_t)((int64_t)d >> 63)`.
- Decoding ZigZag: `(z >> 1) ^ (~(z & 1) + 1)`, i.e. `-(z & 1)` in unsigned arithmetic.
- Varint write: `while (x >= 0x80) { put((x & 0x7F) | 0x80); x >>= 7; } put(x);`.
- Varint read: accumulate `(uint64_t)(b & 0x7F) << shift`, with shift += 7 per byte. A 10th byte may contribute only 1 bit (bit 63).
- A growable byte buffer struct `{uint8_t *data; size_t len, cap;}` keeps the encoder simple.

## Solution
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct { uint8_t *data; size_t len, cap; } Buf;

static void put(Buf *b, uint8_t byte) {
    if (b->len == b->cap) {
        b->cap = b->cap ? b->cap * 2 : 64;
        uint8_t *t = realloc(b->data, b->cap);
        if (!t) { perror("realloc"); exit(1); }
        b->data = t;
    }
    b->data[b->len++] = byte;
}
static void put_varint(Buf *b, uint64_t x) {
    while (x >= 0x80) { put(b, (uint8_t)((x & 0x7F) | 0x80)); x >>= 7; }
    put(b, (uint8_t)x);
}
static uint64_t zigzag(uint64_t n) { return (n << 1) ^ (uint64_t)((int64_t)n >> 63); }
static uint64_t unzigzag(uint64_t z) { return (z >> 1) ^ (~(z & 1) + 1); }

enum { OK, E_TRUNC, E_LONG };
static int get_varint(const uint8_t *p, size_t len, size_t *pos, uint64_t *out) {
    uint64_t x = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
        if (*pos >= len) return E_TRUNC;
        uint8_t b = p[(*pos)++];
        if (i == 9 && b > 1) return E_LONG;            /* only bit 63 is left */
        x |= (uint64_t)(b & 0x7F) << (7 * i);
        if (!(b & 0x80)) { *out = x; return OK; }
    }
    return E_LONG;
}

static int hexval(int c) {
    if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') return c - '0';
    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') return c - 'a' + 10;
    if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F') return c - 'A' + 10;
    return -1;
}

int main(void) {
    char cmd[16];
    while (scanf("%15s", cmd) == 1) {
        if (strcmp(cmd, "encode") == 0) {
            long n;
            if (scanf("%ld", &n) != 1) return 1;
            Buf b = {0};
            put_varint(&b, (uint64_t)n);
            uint64_t prev = 0;
            for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) {
                long long v;
                if (scanf("%lld", &v) != 1) return 1;
                uint64_t cur = (uint64_t)v;
                put_varint(&b, zigzag(i == 0 ? cur : cur - prev));   /* wrap-around delta */
                prev = cur;
            }
            for (size_t i = 0; i < b.len; i++) printf("%02x", b.data[i]);
            long pct = n ? (long)((b.len * 100.0) / (8.0 * n) + 0.5) : 0;
            printf(" (%zu bytes, %ld%%)\n", b.len, pct);
            free(b.data);
        } else if (strcmp(cmd, "decode") == 0) {
            static char hex[1 << 16];
            if (scanf("%65535s", hex) != 1) return 1;
            size_t hl = strlen(hex);
            if (hl % 2) { puts("error: odd hex length"); continue; }
            uint8_t *bytes = malloc(hl / 2 + 1);
            int bad = 0;
            for (size_t i = 0; i < hl / 2; i++) {
                int hi = hexval(hex[2 * i]), lo = hexval(hex[2 * i + 1]);
                if (hi < 0 || lo < 0) { bad = 1; break; }
                bytes[i] = (uint8_t)(hi << 4 | lo);
            }
            if (bad) { puts("error: bad hex digit"); free(bytes); continue; }
            size_t pos = 0, len = hl / 2;
            uint64_t count, z, cur = 0;
            int e = get_varint(bytes, len, &pos, &count);
            Buf out = {0};
            char num[32];
            for (uint64_t i = 0; e == OK && i < count; i++) {
                e = get_varint(bytes, len, &pos, &z);
                if (e != OK) break;
                cur = i == 0 ? unzigzag(z) : cur + unzigzag(z);
                int k = snprintf(num, sizeof num, "%s%lld", i ? " " : "", (long long)(int64_t)cur);
                for (int j = 0; j < k; j++) put(&out, (uint8_t)num[j]);
            }
            if (e == E_TRUNC) puts("error: truncated");
            else if (e == E_LONG) puts("error: varint too long");
            else if (pos != len) puts("error: trailing bytes");
            else { fwrite(out.data, 1, out.len, stdout); putchar('\n'); }
            free(out.data);
            free(bytes);
        }
    }
    return 0;
}
```

**Why this compresses so well:** slowly changing signals have tiny deltas, ZigZag keeps small negative deltas small, and varints store each small number in one byte instead of eight. A smooth encoder log shrinks to about 1/8 of its raw size. The same three tricks are inside Protocol Buffers (varint and ZigZag `sint64`), Parquet and InfluxDB/Gorilla time-series storage, and MAVLink-style telemetry.

**C techniques exercised:** unsigned wrap-around arithmetic to avoid signed-overflow UB, shifts and masks for 7-bit groups, defensive decoding that never reads past the buffer and reports *why* input is malformed, and growable byte buffers. Decoding untrusted bytes safely is the same discipline that prevents parser CVEs.
